Grok Bot, OpenAI dots, Claude Duet.

All three are the same idea: an agent that works in the background and only taps you when a decision is yours.

The catch is where they live. All three run on someone else's computer.

AnyModelBot is the open-source version of that idea.

MIT licensed. 3,109 stars, +315 today. Runs on your own Windows, Mac or Linux box.

One key reaches 70+ models. GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM.

Swap models per conversation, or bring your own API keys and skip the middleman entirely.

Each bot gets its own persona, workspace and memory. Memory is just Markdown files on your disk.

It does real work. Files, commands, background tasks, scheduled rules like "check this price every morning and only tell me if it drops."

Every task has a $1 budget by default. Anything outside its workspace stops for your approval first.

The honest part: "local-first" covers your files and memory, not your prompts. Model calls go through Modelflare and get logged. The README says so plainly.

The app itself is free, no subscription. Models are pay per use, from $0.4 per million input tokens.

https://t.co/AhVVxtiDVt

note_tweet.text:
AnyModelBot: Putting Personal AI Agent Back on Your Computer

What it wants to solve is not "finding another chat window", but "keeping the resident AI on its own machine".

A robot is a human design with its own default model, workspace, memory and avatar; Permission is divided into three grades: read-only, workspace and full permission. When you get out of the workspace, play the approval card and wait for you to nod. It can read and write files, execute commands in the sandbox, send the results back to chat as files, and also use the built-in Cua Driver to operate the desktop. Reading the screen does not need approval, and clicking and typing can require confirmation one by one. It can also import skill packages with SKILL.md and pull several robots into the same group chat. In addition to the application, WeChat scan code, flying book, Telegram, Slack and Discord can all find the same robot, and the account is shared globally.

What is more interesting about it is that it extends the "dialogue" to "watch for you": the memory is stored in this machine with three layers of Markdown, which is separated by team, robot and group. When the context is almost full, the context manager compresses or opens a new dialogue with a handover summary; Background tasks take on long tasks. Check the rules by yourself, and only push them to you if there is something worth saying. Don't disturb the time, the daily news limit and the budget of each task are written into the settings. The sidebar line "Need you" only appears when you really want to make a decision.

DeepSeek Harness and Super Agent prototype are behind, Electron desktop application is in the foreground, and there are also command lines, Docker and a web console that only listens to this machine. A Modelflare account on the model side covers 70+ GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, etc., and can also fill in the official Key direct manufacturers; Compared with the resident agents such as Grok Bot, OpenAI dots and Claude Duet, the difference lies in MIT's open source, running on its own devices, and paying by volume without binding subscriptions.

The boundary is also straightforward: the request to take Modelflare is kept by the server, and the official Key is directly connected without forwarding; The computer operation of macOS is still Beta, while Telegram, Slack and Discord only deal with single chat at present.

For those who want to move the agent from "other people's cloud" to "their own desktop", this scheme can really land: first, take back the resident AI, and then turn what you get back into a portable adjustable entrance.

Source: github | "model flare-ai/anymodelbot"
